image_description: A close-up, slightly low-angle shot of a dual-headed traffic light assembly mounted on a metal pole. The left signal head shows an illuminated red light at the top, with two unlit lenses below (appearing blueish/dark). The right signal head shows an illuminated amber/yellow light at the top and a red light in the middle, with one unlit lens below. The housing is gray/metallic with visors over each lens. The background features a street scene with parked cars (a blue van and a silver sedan) and a building facade, all rendered with a painterly, textured aesthetic.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The entire image exhibits a strong 'painterly' or 'oil painting' texture filter. While this may be stylistic intent, in the context of AI generation auditing, it often masks underlying structural defects. The textures on the cars and building lack photographic realism, appearing smudged or brush-stroked.

The blue van on the left has distorted geometry; the wheel wells and door lines do not align logically. The silver car on the right has a melted rear bumper and indistinct license plate area. These are classic AI artifacts where complex mechanical objects lose structural coherence.
The two signal heads are mounted side-by-side but seem to attach to the pole at slightly different angles and depths, creating a subtle spatial inconsistency in how they connect to the central mast.
The license plate on the silver car in the background is illegible gibberish, a common artifact where AI fails to render coherent text strings.
